terms.gloss: a parapet, a balustrade: a guardrail
terms.comment: A breastwork or parapet on towers and ramparts in Caesar, and in Vitruvius the balustrade between two columns (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens gives it for a railing. So it serves for the guardrail of a scaffold.
A closer ancient word for a parapet.

phrases.latin: ferrum trānsversum ad marginem tabulātī positum
phrases.english: a metal rail placed at the edge of the deck

sources: Lewis & Short: pluteus · Lewis & Short: lorica
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. banister, balustrade, railing.
